chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

«Zihar does not take effect except upon the sin (of the husband); so when he has sinned, he is not permitted to have sexual relations with her until he expiates. If he was ignorant and had relations, then only one expiation is upon him.»

key_terms.الظِّهَارُ: Zihar, a form of irrevocable divorce in Shia jurisprudence where the husband declares his wife unlawful for intercourse like his mother's back.
key_terms.الْحِنْثُ: The sin or fault incurred by the husband for pronouncing Zihar.
key_terms.يُوَاقِعَهَا: To have sexual relations with her.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Zihar and its expiation if a husband has sexual relations with his wife?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith clarifies that Zihar is a vow of abstinence rather than a final divorce, requiring specific expiation to resume marital relations. It distinguishes between intentional violation, which necessitates expiation before intercourse, and unintentional violation, where a single expiation suffices, reflecting the principle of leniency for the ignorant (jahil). This ruling underscores the importance of intentionality in ritual obligations within the Ja'fari school.
